absent: Complete memory layout and locking for callback segment lists beyond enablement and count behavior
Grace period sequence allocation wrap recovery and full tick dependency lifecycle
Priority boost thread scheduling wake conditions and mutex ownership transfer details
Torture operation vector contracts histogram binning and stall check thresholds
Exact interrupt preemption and configuration guards for helpers defined outside these fragments

findings.text: Deferred quiescent state completion on read unlock with interrupt restore consumes pending task and CPU requests and guarantees interrupts are restored on every exit. It requires disabled interrupts on entry, treats task special flags as stable, clears both task and defer markers when present, ensures normal and expedited needs are forwarded through per CPU and hierarchy reporting, and when the task had blocked it unlinks the task from its leaf node and triggers upward propagation if that node became quiescent.

Normal grace period completion propagates from leaf nodes toward the root by clearing membership bits, marking nodes whose CPUs and blocked readers have all checked in, and signalling the grace period thread only when the root becomes fully quiescent. A report is ignored when its sequence no longer matches the current period or its bit is already clear, and an unblock path performs the same upward walk when removal of the last blocked reader empties a leaf.

Expedited completion propagates by clearing per CPU need indicators and then clearing node expedited masks upward, waking the expedited waiter only when the root has no remaining tasks or mask bits. When a node still has blocked tasks but no outstanding CPU bits, control transfers to priority boost initiation rather than continuing upward, and per CPU tick dependencies for expedited waits are released as their CPUs are cleared.

A task that blocks inside a read section remains queued on the leaf node where it first blocked, with distinct head pointers identifying the first normal, expedited and boost entries and a successor link that yields null at the list tail. Removal reinitializes the task linkage, clears its blocked node association, advances any head pointer that referenced the removed task to its successor, and treats absence of a normal head as absence of blocked readers in the preemptible configuration.

Per CPU quiescent reports are valid only for the grace period in which they were recorded. A mismatch of recorded and current sequences, a pending wrap indication, or a still asserted need flag causes the report to be dropped and the need flag to be reasserted for the new period, without touching hierarchy masks, while an already cleared hierarchy bit likewise results in no upward action.

Hierarchy reporting serializes each node with its dedicated spin lock with interrupts disabled, asserting ownership on entry and releasing exactly once on every exit path, including early completions. Hand off between levels releases the child before acquiring the parent except for the leaf unblock path which keeps interrupts disabled across the transfer, and the root completion path releases the root lock before waking the grace period thread.

Priority boost coordination snapshots boost mutex ownership while holding the node lock and releases the mutex only after the node lock has been dropped. Boost initiation itself always releases the node lock before returning, whether or not it wakes the boost thread, and the deferred unlock path only attempts mutex release when the snapshot showed current task ownership.

Observed node state comprises period sequencing and completion markers, normal and expedited pending CPU masks, group membership and parent linkage, hierarchy coordinates and CPU range bounds, blocked task list heads for normal expedited and boost cohorts, plus boost thread identity status and timing and an expedited wait queue at the global level.

Observed per CPU state comprises defer pending marker, normal and expedited need indicators with a combined view, recorded period sequence and wrap flag, leaf association and group mask, core quiescent need flag, urgency and heavy quiescent flags, forced tick indicators for normal and expedited waits, CPU identity, and a segmented callback list with enablement and count queries.

Observed task state comprises a combined unlock special word with need and blocked components, a pointer to the leaf node on which the task is blocked, an intrusive list element linking blocked tasks on that node, and a process identifier used for tracing unlock events.

Several predicates have build dependent forms. Blocked reader presence and deferred need evaluation collapse to constant absence in non preemptible builds, local quiescent recording either only clears normal need or additionally forwards expedited need depending on flavor, boost initiation is either conditional wake logic or an unconditional unlock, and strict grace period builds add synchronous reporting plus a small delay on the unlock path.

Externally reachable reporting services include deferred unlock completion with interrupt restore, leaf unblock reporting, per CPU normal reporting, per CPU expedited reporting through the deferred and need paths, and a forward progress diagnostic that summarizes grace period age and pending callback distribution.

Diagnostic warnings flag inconsistent hierarchy state such as a task associated with a non leaf or changed node, completion markers equalling current sequence while readers or mask bits remain, upward reports arriving for an already finished period, per CPU reports executing on the wrong CPU, and torture progress shortfalls where version and sequence advances are smaller than expected.

Forward progress torture exercises liveness through complementary loops plus an out of memory escape. One loop repeatedly acquires and releases read sections with scheduling opportunities and then checks version and sequence progress, another continuously enqueues callbacks and reclaims completed ones until enough multi period launders accumulate or a time or stop condition fires, and the memory pressure handler serializes histogram capture, forces an emergency stop visible across CPUs, then repeatedly frees and barrier drains before reporting success.

Callback backlog accounting returns zero when the per CPU segmented list is disabled and otherwise returns its queued count, and the progress diagnostic distinguishes an in progress grace period by reporting its age and thread state from an idle period by reporting time since last completion plus a stall probe, followed by a sparse per CPU listing of nonzero backlog counts and their maximum.

Coordination relies on named symbolic values for defer pending marking, grace period force scan request flagging, normal and expedited tick dependency bits, and notifier success reporting, each referenced by the fragments without exposing numeric encoding here.

Successful normal quiescent reporting clears both urgent and heavy quiescent requests, and for full tickless CPUs it additionally releases the tick dependency and clears the forced tick marker when that marker was set, with the caller holding the associated leaf lock.
